Bulgaria’s Budget 2025: Key Announcements and Priorities Bulgaria’s budget for 2025 is set to be finalized next⁢ week , as announced by Social Minister Borislav Gutsanov during a recent ​event in Burgas. The⁢ minister emphasized that​ the general program for the country’s⁤ management will be ready with specific priorities outlined.
Gutsanov assured that there will be no tax⁤ increases or fee hikes,⁣ and there will be no ​reduction⁣ in funds allocated for social ⁢benefits in ‌the​ upcoming budget. This assurance comes in response to ‍requests from trade unions to increase funds ​for food vouchers, which will be discussed in upcoming meetings with⁤ the unions.
Restricted food‌ mark-ups were highlighted by Gutsanov as a critical issue. He noted that the price ‍of a product can increase nearly tenfold from the manufacturer to the store, underscoring the need for regulatory measures to control these ⁢mark-ups.
The minister also pointed out that budget holes can be filled by targeting the​ “grey sector” . He stressed the importance of the National revenue Agency (NRA) and customs in this effort, stating that their cooperation is essential to‍ prevent a sharp decline in state revenue​ and GDP.
in⁤ related news, National Assembly Chairman ‌Natalia⁢ Kiselova announced that the⁣ nomination procedures for various regulators ‌are expected to be⁢ on the parliament’s agenda next⁤ week. She noted that⁢ several bodies, such as ⁣the‍ Dossier Commission, have been expired since 2017 and need to be addressed ‍urgently.
regarding the proposal to ban the sale of e-cigarettes , Kiselova emphasized the need to first assess how current controls are being exercised to prevent the sale of such devices to minors. The Health Committee will consider the bill, taking into account both parental and authoritative controls.
